title: Atomic module cache publication
objective: Publish compiler module cache files atomically and prove concurrent readers, writers, and bounded pruning never observe partial entries or delete actively leased publications

oracles: deterministic temporary-directory concurrent publication and cleanup tests

handoff.summary: Publishes both compiler-generated imported-module metadata and lazy runtime JavaScript/bytecode cache documents through a shared same-directory temporary-file-and-rename primitive. Concurrent publishers can replace one complete cache value with another, while readers never observe a truncated JSON document. Publication failures remain advisory cache misses, and private temporary files are removed on failure. Temporary-root regressions exercise four concurrent large publishers plus readers, failure cleanup, and an active leased publisher racing applied bounded cleanup; the established compiler and REPL cache integration suite also passes.
risks: The full compiler tier has an unrelated existing matrix fixture failure because its standalone runtime cannot import sagejs.linear_algebra.matrix_vector_public.
The full integration tier has an unrelated existing higher-weight Hecke failure because p1_gcd is absent from the published native artifact set in this worktree.

Windows, macOS arm64, and Linux arm64 were not available in this lane; the implementation uses only Node's cross-platform exclusive create, write, close, rename, and unlink primitives and should be exercised by platform CI.
next_steps: Integrate the focused cache publication change and let ordinary platform CI exercise the helper on Windows and arm64 hosts.
